<!--
Appendix S3: definition of the hotspot threshold and metrics of the native
hotspots (area, present-day hotspot cells lost, invasive species in the present-day
hotspot cells, extrapolation), with their sensitivity
to the hotspot threshold and to the species with poorly validated models.
Self-contained: the richness curve and the tables are computed in this document from the
binary maps of the species distribution models, and only the PDF is saved.

Inputs : results/SDMs/<species>/03_projections/rep<r>/binary/ and binary/ (replicate and
         consensus maps, written by 04_SDMs.R)
         results/SDMs/summary_evaluation.csv (spatial validation, 04_SDMs.R)
         results/extrapolation/novel_<scenario>.tif (04_SDMs.R)
Output : S3_hotspots_supplementary.pdf, next to this file
Knit with the "Knit" button. The working directory is this folder
(results/supplementary/), so paths to the rest of the repository start with ../..
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(terra)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
# kableExtra would load many extra LaTeX packages (tabu, multirow, wrapfig...) that
# must be installed in the LaTeX distribution; only the few packages needed by these
# tables are loaded (see header-includes in the YAML header above)
options(kableExtra.latex.load_packages = FALSE)
library(kableExtra)

PROJECT_ROOT <- "../.."   # this document is in results/supplementary/
source(file.path(PROJECT_ROOT, "src", "figure_common.R"), local = knitr::knit_global())   # palette, theme, species lists and hotspot functions

options(knitr.kable.NA = "")      # empty cell instead of NA in tables

# Tables are written directly in LaTeX (not as pandoc tables) so that scale_down can shrink
# the wide ones to the page width; booktabs rules, no extra space every five rows
options(knitr.table.format = "latex")
kable <- function(...) knitr::kable(..., booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "")
```

```{r analysis}
# Native species richness in the present (number of species predicted present per cell)
richness_present <- load_richness(NATIVE_SPECIES, "present")

# Area of the hotspot of the consensus maps (the one shown in the figures)
consensus_km2 <- as.numeric(global(cellSize(richness_present, unit = "km") *
                                     (richness_present >= HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD),
                                   "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1])

# Number of grid cells at each native richness level (present) and percentage
# change with respect to the previous richness level
curve <- as.data.frame(table(values(richness_present))) %>%
  rename(richness = Var1, n_cells = Freq) %>%
  mutate(richness = as.integer(as.character(richness))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(richness), richness > 0) %>%
  arrange(richness) %>%
  mutate(pct_change = round(100 * (n_cells - lag(n_cells)) / lag(n_cells), 1))

# Metrics of the native hotspots with each final-model replicate, for the threshold used in
# the analyses and for thresholds from 5 to 8 native species (sensitivity)
thresholds <- HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD + (-2:1)
m_all <- hotspot_metrics(thresholds)
m <- m_all %>% filter(threshold == HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD)
n_reps <- sum(m$scenario == "present")
n_consensus <- ceiling(n_reps / 2)

# Sensitivity to the species with poorly validated models: species whose spatial
# validation TSS (RF, mean of the folds) is below TSS_MIN are excluded. If native species
# are excluded, the hotspot threshold is lowered by the same number, so that a hotspot
# still allows the same number of absent native species.
TSS_MIN <- 0.4
validation <- read.csv(file.path(DIR_SDM, "summary_evaluation.csv"))
weak <- validation %>%
  filter(algo == "RF", metric.eval == "TSS", mean < TSS_MIN) %>%
  mutate(Species = gsub(" ", "_", Species))
weak_native   <- intersect(NATIVE_SPECIES, weak$Species)
weak_invasive <- intersect(INVASIVE_SPECIES, weak$Species)
sens_native   <- setdiff(NATIVE_SPECIES, weak_native)
sens_invasive <- setdiff(INVASIVE_SPECIES, weak_invasive)
sens_threshold <- HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD - length(weak_native)
m_sens <- if (length(weak$Species) > 0) {
  hotspot_metrics(sens_threshold, native_species = sens_native, invasive_species = sens_invasive)
} else NULL
```

# Methods notes

```{r methods-note, results='asis'}
cat(
  "Native hotspots were defined as the cells where at least n of the nine native species are ",
  "predicted present. The threshold (n = ", HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD, ") was selected from the distribution ",
  "of present-day native richness: it is the last richness level before the first transition between ",
  "consecutive levels with a decline in the number of cells greater than 50% (Table 1, Figures 1 and 2).\n\n",
  "Three metrics were calculated for the native hotspots in each scenario, as in the main text: ",
  "(i) the hotspot area; (ii) the percentage of the present-day hotspot cells that are no longer ",
  "hotspot; and (iii) the mean number of invasive species (out of nine) in the present-day hotspot ",
  "cells under each scenario, which measures the exposure of the current refugia themselves. The future ",
  "metrics refer only to the native hotspots, because the question addressed is the fate of the ",
  "native refugia; invasive hotspots are shown only for the present (main text, Figure 3).\n\n",
  "The final model of each species was fitted ", n_reps, " times, each with its own random set of ",
  "pseudo-absences and its own seed (replicates; Appendix S2). Every metric was ",
  "calculated separately with each replicate (replicate r of all species), and the changes with ",
  "respect to the present were calculated within each replicate. Tables give the mean of the ",
  "replicates, the minimum and maximum among them in brackets, and the number of replicates in which ",
  "the metric increases. The maps of the figures are the consensus of the replicates (a cell is ",
  "predicted present if at least ", n_consensus, " of the ", n_reps, " replicates predict it); the hotspot ",
  "threshold was selected on the consensus maps.\n\n",
  "Three further checks are reported: the percentage of hotspot cells where some predictor is outside ",
  "its present-day range (extrapolation); the metrics recalculated with hotspot thresholds from ",
  min(thresholds), " to ", max(thresholds), " native species; and the metrics recalculated without the ",
  "species whose models had a spatial validation TSS below ", TSS_MIN, ".\n\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

# Richness distribution and threshold selection

```{r curve-table}
kable(curve %>% mutate(pct_change = ifelse(is.na(pct_change), NA, sprintf("%+.1f", pct_change))),
      col.names = c("Richness (n species)", "N grid cells", "% change vs. previous level"),
      caption = "Distribution of grid-cell counts across native richness levels (present-day).") %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = "striped")
```

```{r curve-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Number of grid cells at each level of native species richness (present-day). Dark bars: hotspot cells."}
curve$class <- factor(ifelse(curve$richness >= HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD, "Hotspot", "Presence area"),
                      levels = c("Presence area", "Hotspot"))

ggplot(curve, aes(x = factor(richness), y = n_cells, fill = class)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "black", linewidth = LINE_WIDTH) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Presence area" = COL[["native_presence"]],
                               "Hotspot" = COL[["native_hotspot"]]), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Native species richness per cell", y = "Number of grid cells") +
  theme_fig()
```

```{r drop-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Percentage change in the number of grid cells relative to the previous richness level. Dark bar: the hotspot threshold; dashed line: -50%."}
drop_df <- curve %>% filter(!is.na(pct_change))
drop_df$class <- factor(ifelse(drop_df$richness == HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD, "Hotspot threshold", "Other levels"),
                        levels = c("Other levels", "Hotspot threshold"))

ggplot(drop_df, aes(x = factor(richness), y = pct_change, fill = class)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "black", linewidth = LINE_WIDTH) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -50, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = LINE_WIDTH) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Other levels" = COL[["native_presence"]],
                               "Hotspot threshold" = COL[["native_hotspot"]]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Richness level (n species)", y = "% change in cell count vs. previous level") +
  theme_fig()
```

```{r drop-note, results='asis'}
# Criterion: FIRST transition (from lower to higher richness) whose percentage
# change is below -50%. It is not the largest drop of the whole series (between
# the last two levels, based on very few cells), which would not identify the
# level at which the decline starts to accelerate.
drop_limit <- -50

cut_point <- drop_df %>%
  filter(pct_change < drop_limit) %>%
  slice_min(richness, n = 1)

if (nrow(cut_point) == 0) {

  cat(sprintf(
    "No transition between consecutive richness levels exceeds a %d%% decline in cell count; the threshold used in the analyses is n = %d.\n\n",
    abs(drop_limit), HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD))

} else {

  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      "The decline in cell count becomes markedly steeper starting at the ",
      "transition from richness level %d to %d (a change of %.1f%%), the first ",
      "transition exceeding a %d%% decline, compared to more moderate changes ",
      "(%+.1f%% to %+.1f%%) across all preceding richness levels. The threshold ",
      "n = %d was therefore selected as the last richness level before this ",
      "marked acceleration in decline.\n\n"
    ),
    cut_point$richness - 1, cut_point$richness, cut_point$pct_change,
    abs(drop_limit),
    min(drop_df$pct_change[drop_df$richness < cut_point$richness], na.rm = TRUE),
    max(drop_df$pct_change[drop_df$richness < cut_point$richness], na.rm = TRUE),
    cut_point$richness - 1
  ))

  if (cut_point$richness - 1 != HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "NOTE: the threshold used in the analyses (n = %d) differs from the one identified by this criterion.\n\n",
      HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD))
  }
}
```

# Native hotspots and invasive species

```{r metric-helpers}
# Add the change with respect to the present within each replicate
with_changes <- function(d) {
  d %>% group_by(version) %>%
    mutate(area_change = 100 * (native_km2 / native_km2[scenario == "present"] - 1),
           fixed_change = inv_fixed - inv_fixed[scenario == "present"]) %>%
    ungroup()
}
mm <- with_changes(m)

# "mean [minimum to maximum among replicates]" for one scenario and variable
with_range <- function(d, sc, var, digits, sign = FALSE) {
  x <- d[[var]][d$scenario == sc]
  f <- paste0("%", if (sign) "+" else "", ".", digits, "f")
  sprintf(paste0(f, " [", f, " to ", f, "]"), mean(x), min(x), max(x))
}

# Number of replicates in which the metric increases
n_up <- function(d, sc, var) paste0(sum(d[[var]][d$scenario == sc] > 0), " of ", n_reps)
```

```{r hotspot-table}
hotspot_table <- data.frame(
  Scenario = unname(SCENARIO_LABELS),
  area     = sapply(names(SCENARIO_LABELS), function(s) with_range(mm, s, "native_km2", 0)),
  change   = c("", sapply(FUTURE_KEYS, function(s) with_range(mm, s, "area_change", 0, sign = TRUE))),
  up       = c("", sapply(FUTURE_KEYS, function(s) n_up(mm, s, "area_change"))),
  lost     = c("", sapply(FUTURE_KEYS, function(s) with_range(mm, s, "lost_pct", 1))),
  row.names = NULL
)

kable(hotspot_table,
      col.names = c("Scenario", "Area (km\u00b2)", "Change in area (%)",
                    paste0("Increase (of ", n_reps, ")"), "Hotspot cells lost (%)"),
      caption = paste0("Native hotspots (at least ", HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD, " of 9 native species) in each scenario: mean of the replicates and, in brackets, minimum to maximum among them. Changes are calculated within each replicate. Increase: number of replicates, out of ", n_reps, ", in which the area increases. Hotspot cells lost: present-day hotspot cells that are no longer hotspot.")) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "scale_down", "hold_position"))
```

```{r consensus-note, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "The present-day hotspot of the consensus maps (main text, Figure 3) covers %s km\u00b2, ",
  "whereas the mean of the replicates in Table 2 is %s km\u00b2 (range %s to %s). The two areas ",
  "are computed in different orders: in the consensus map each species is first reduced to the ",
  "cells where at least %d of the %d replicates predict it, and the hotspot is then defined on the ",
  "sum of those maps; in Table 2 the hotspot is defined within each replicate and its area is then ",
  "averaged. Because a hotspot requires %d species at the same time, a cell where most species are ",
  "predicted in most, but not all, replicates is a hotspot in the consensus map but only in some ",
  "replicates. The consensus map is used for the figures and the replicates for the metrics, which ",
  "carry their uncertainty and allow the changes to be paired within each replicate.\n\n"),
  format(round(consensus_km2), big.mark = ","),
  format(round(mean(mm$native_km2[mm$scenario == "present"])), big.mark = ","),
  format(round(min(mm$native_km2[mm$scenario == "present"])), big.mark = ","),
  format(round(max(mm$native_km2[mm$scenario == "present"])), big.mark = ","),
  n_consensus, n_reps, HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD))
```

# Sensitivity to the hotspot threshold

```{r sensitivity-helpers}
thr_labels <- paste0("n = ", thresholds)
by_n <- lapply(thresholds, function(n) with_changes(m_all %>% filter(threshold == n)))

# mean change and replicates in which it is an increase
change_cell <- function(d, sc, var, digits) {
  x <- d[[var]][d$scenario == sc]
  sprintf(paste0("%+.", digits, "f (%d of %d)"), mean(x), sum(x > 0), length(x))
}
level_cell <- function(d, sc, var, digits) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), mean(d[[var]][d$scenario == sc]))

table_over_n <- function(present_fun, future_fun) {
  rows <- c("present", FUTURE_KEYS)
  out <- data.frame(Scenario = unname(SCENARIO_LABELS[rows]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (i in seq_along(thresholds)) {
    out[[thr_labels[i]]] <- sapply(rows, function(s) {
      if (s == "present") present_fun(by_n[[i]]) else future_fun(by_n[[i]], s)
    })
  }
  out
}
head_n <- c(" " = 1, setNames(length(thresholds), "Hotspot threshold (number of native species)"))
```

```{r sensitivity-area}
kable(table_over_n(function(d) level_cell(d, "present", "native_km2", 0),
                   function(d, s) change_cell(d, s, "area_change", 0)),
      row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Area of the native hotspots with other thresholds: mean area in the present (square kilometres) and mean change in area with respect to the present (percent); in brackets, number of replicates in which the area increases.") %>%
  add_header_above(head_n) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "scale_down", "hold_position"))
```

```{r sensitivity-lost}
lost_table <- table_over_n(function(d) "",
                           function(d, s) with_range(d, s, "lost_pct", 1))[-1, ]

kable(lost_table, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Present-day native hotspot cells lost (percent) with other thresholds: mean of the replicates and, in brackets, minimum to maximum among them.") %>%
  add_header_above(head_n) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "scale_down", "hold_position"))
```

```{r sensitivity-fixed}
kable(table_over_n(function(d) level_cell(d, "present", "inv_fixed", 2),
                   function(d, s) change_cell(d, s, "fixed_change", 2)),
      row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Invasive species in the present-day native hotspot cells with other thresholds: mean in the present and mean change with respect to the present; in brackets, number of replicates in which it increases.") %>%
  add_header_above(head_n) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "scale_down", "hold_position"))
```

# Sensitivity to the species with poorly validated models

```{r species-sensitivity, results='asis'}
if (is.null(m_sens)) {
  cat(sprintf("All species have a spatial validation TSS of at least %.1f; no sensitivity analysis is needed.\n\n", TSS_MIN))
} else {
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "Species with a spatial validation TSS below %.1f (Appendix S2): %s. ",
    "The metrics were recalculated without them: native hotspots with %d native species and a ",
    "threshold of %d (so that, as in the main analysis, at most %d native species may be absent ",
    "from a hotspot cell), and invasive richness out of %d invasive species.\n\n"),
    TSS_MIN,
    paste(sprintf("*%s*", species_display(weak$Species)), collapse = ", "),
    length(sens_native), sens_threshold, length(NATIVE_SPECIES) - HOTSPOT_THRESHOLD,
    length(sens_invasive)))
}
```

```{r species-sensitivity-table}
if (!is.null(m_sens)) {
  ms <- with_changes(m_sens)
  sens_table <- data.frame(
    Scenario = unname(SCENARIO_LABELS[FUTURE_KEYS]),
    area     = sapply(FUTURE_KEYS, function(s) change_cell(ms, s, "area_change", 0)),
    lost     = sapply(FUTURE_KEYS, function(s) with_range(ms, s, "lost_pct", 1)),
    fixed    = sapply(FUTURE_KEYS, function(s) change_cell(ms, s, "fixed_change", 2)),
    row.names = NULL
  )
  kable(sens_table,
        col.names = c("Scenario", "Change in area (%)", "Hotspot cells lost (%)",
                      "Invasive species in present-day hotspot cells (change)"),
        caption = paste0("Native hotspot metrics without the species with poorly validated models: mean of the replicates; in brackets, number of replicates (out of ", n_reps, ") in which the metric increases, or minimum to maximum for the hotspot cells lost. Present-day values: hotspot area ",
                         round(mean(ms$native_km2[ms$scenario == "present"])), " km\u00b2; ",
                         sprintf("%.2f", mean(ms$inv_fixed[ms$scenario == "present"])), " invasive species per hotspot cell.")) %>%
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "scale_down", "hold_position"))
}
```
